extracted.intended_audience: United Way communications staff, local United Ways, designers, and external agencies/vendors creating branded materials and press/marketing collateral
extracted.subtask_description: Visual identity and brand guidelines for United Way communications, covering logo usage, color palette & accessibility, typography, photography, graphic elements, iconography, and messaging (impact areas) to ensure consistent branded materials and press collateral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary logo (Circle of Hope + logotype)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our primary logo consists of the logo symbol, the Circle of Hope, and our logotype, which is our name set in customized type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The logo symbol (Circle of Hope) should always appear in its entirety and never be deconstructed. The logotype has been refreshed; the symbol and logotype have been removed from the rectangular holding shape to convey an open, inclusive, dynamic approach. The logo has been repositioned and re-rendered for greater utility and legibility and optimized for small spaces and digital media. See 'Our Brand Architecture' for how to localize the logo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo structure (holding shape removed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The logo symbol and logotype have been removed from the rectangular holding shape to better convey our open, inclusive and dynamic approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not recreate or reintroduce the rectangular holding shape; use the updated structure to optimize for small spaces and digital media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo arrangements (horizontal vs vertical; symbol-only for small spaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our horizontal logo is our preferred version. The vertical logo works best for vertical layouts to optimize space and legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full logo in all contexts except for small spaces (e.g., favicon or social media icon), where the logo symbol may be used on its own. Prefer horizontal where possible; use vertical for vertical layouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo variations (full-color, knockout, one-color)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full-Color (Preferred); Knockout (White) for dark backgrounds; One-Color Version (Black) for grayscale or one-color printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full-color version is preferred and should be used whenever possible. Do not adjust the colors of the logo symbol in any way. The United Way logotype is blue unless there is low contrast with the background, in which case it should be white. Ensure sufficient contrast for clarity and legibility when used with photography. Use knockout (white) on dark backgrounds or photos where full-color won't work. Use one-color black where full-color or knockout won't provide sufficient contrast or for one-color printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo usage over photography
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the United Way logo over photography, ensure there is sufficient contrast between the background and logo for optimal clarity and legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the photograph is very busy or has low contrast, use a gradient between the photo and the logo. Steps: place the photo in your document; add a gradient and set it to Multiply in Blending Mode; add a version of the logo in a section of the photo with enough contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color palette (primary, secondary, tertiary and tones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary colors are derived from the logo symbol: blue, red and yellow, each with four shades. Secondary color is green; tertiary colors are purple and black. White is universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary colors (one, two or all three) should be applied across all communications (unless black & white). Tones can add texture and depth but must not replace primary colors. Secondary and tertiary colors should be used as accents or in data visualization and not as the main/dominant color. Refer to the Bringing the Elements to Life section for color application examples. Specific RGB/HEX/CMYK/Pantone values are provided for each color and shade—use those exact values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color accessibility / contrast standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved color combinations meet the level AA standards of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always promote visibility and legibility by ensuring sufficient contrast for text/background. Use an online tool (e.g., Adobe Color Contrast Analyzer) to check contrast ratios. The guide lists approved combinations and notes size thresholds (Text 18pt and above / 14pt bold and above for certain color uses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary colors dominance in application
rubrics_metrics.description: All core communications should prominently feature at least one, but preferably all three, primary colors as the dominant color(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary color tones can add texture and depth but should not replace or overshadow primary colors. Secondary and tertiary colors may be used as supporting elements to enhance visual interest, but should not take precedence over primary colors. Examples demonstrate using primary colors as focal points with secondary/tertiary accents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography — brand fonts and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Antonio is the brand font for headlines; Palanquin is the brand font for body copy. Alternate brand font: Noto. Default system font: Arial. Special use font: Monte Carlo Script for events/fundraising collateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antonio and Palanquin are available at fonts.google.com. In languages where Antonio/Palanquin are not available, use Noto. When primary and alternative fonts are unavailable, use Arial (widely supported by OS and browsers). Monte Carlo Script is reserved for more sophisticated event collateral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography usage and hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to apply fonts and weights to create messaging hierarchy: Headlines (Antonio Bold), Sub-headlines (Palanquin SemiBold), Body copy (Palanquin Regular), Pull quotes (Palanquin Bold), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italics are not recommended because they appear disruptive with Antonio; if absolutely necessary, use italics of the alternate brand font (Noto). Follow provided font-weight examples and sizes to maintain consistent hierarchy and legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography guidelines (selection, tone, and avoidances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photography should be community-rooted, responsive, highlight people in action, be engaging, energizing, and elevating, and showcase people connecting to their community and each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-generated photography and/or people-based illustrations should never be used as a substitute for place-based, people-focused imagery. Avoid: photos that are out of focus; photos with unnatural/extreme filters or effects; overly posed photos; photos on blank backgrounds/silhouetted without context; low resolution or poor quality images; overly busy/complex composition; AI-generated images or people-based illustrations. Add captions when necessary (left-aligned, below the photo).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic elements configuration (circle/arc/arrow usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic elements inspired by the logo symbol should advance the brand story; prioritize the circle and arc as heroic components and use the arrow as a supportive element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use elements in 'Connective' arrangements (overlapping arc/arrow/circle to depict an interconnected approach), 'Responsive' arrangements (dynamic arrangements to evoke movement and proactive solutions), and 'Scalable' uses (ripple effects to mirror cascading impact). Prioritize circle and arc visually; arrow signals points of impact and complements communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconography style and color usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Iconography is a simple line treatment with rounded edges to mirror radiating lines in the logo symbol; icons are functional for navigation and comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Icons should be optimized for legibility and clarity in small spaces. Icons may be rendered in any of the primary colors; ideally a set of icons should be displayed in the same primary color. Ensure proper contrast between icon and background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact areas — consistent messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate consistently the four key impact areas: Healthy Community; Youth Opportunity; Financial Security; Community Resiliency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, communicate these impact areas jointly to help audiences understand breadth and depth of impact. Use the provided defined labels and sample program lists for each impact area to maintain consistency across communications.
